A1.justification: Both readable 12-page PDFs describe the same DVD-Quant work and support reliable comparison. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement; both reference a separate supplementary file that is not supplied. Pages 2–12 are textually and visually identical.

before.justification: v2 reports original video-generation evaluations, component ablations, threshold experiments, and memory/latency measurements in Section 4, Tables 1–5, and Figure 6.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical evaluations, ablations, threshold experiments, and efficiency measurements in Section 4, Tables 1–5, and Figure 6.

M1.justification: BGR, ARQ, and δ-Guided Bit Switching retain identical procedures. Section 3, Algorithm 1, and the method equations are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain the same VBench text-to-video evaluation coverage. The statement about evaluating Wan2.1 in a separate supplementary file is also unchanged; no new data, tasks, or test scenarios appear in the supplied PDFs.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the BF16 baseline, MinMax, SmoothQuant, Quarot, and ViDiT-Q. Table 2 retains the same STP, ITP, ABS, and SBA mixed-precision comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains 50-step flow matching, CFG scale 6.0, flow shift 7.0, and eight VBench metrics. Precision configurations and the mixed-precision comparison procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The layer-error and activation analyses in Figures 3–4, mixed-precision comparison in Table 2, BGR/ARQ ablations in Table 3, and threshold sensitivity study in Figure 6 are identical.

E5.justification: Both use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains DVD-Quant W4A4 aesthetic/imaging quality of 61.96/61.82, and Table 5 retains its 2.12× latency speedup.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains identical mathematical definitions and reasoning, including the quantization objective, refinement updates, rotation/scaling formulation, and bit-switching rule in Equations 1–11.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three-component data-free framework, approximately 2× speedup claim, and claimed first successful W4A4 post-training quantization for Video DiTs.

C2.justification: Interpretations of BGR/ARQ synergy, online activation scaling, the threshold quality/resource trade-off, and compatibility with TeaCache are unchanged. No substantive limitations or qualifications are added.

D1.justification: The RTX4090 hardware disclosure, experimental settings, GEMM-kernel explanation, and promised code/model release at the same repository remain unchanged. No technical or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and positioning against calibration-based quantization methods are identical.

P1.justification: Page 1 changes the corresponding-author designation from Yulun Zhang and Linghe Kong to Xiaokang Yang, updating author markers and the contact footnote. The arXiv version/date stamp also changes. Narrative text and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6, Tables 1–5, captions, placement, and page layout are unchanged. Visual differences are confined to the page-1 correspondence text and version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: v3 changes correspondence information and the version/date stamp while preserving the scientific content, evidence, explanations, and result displays. These administrative edits establish no meaningful net difference in paper quality.
